findings.reason: an implementer cannot satisfy both readings; taken literally §10 removes the bookend reserve from every metered group (stripping verify's protection that §8 says the reserve exists for) and voids the "fifth expires unspent" premise the lift is motivated by, so the plan must state which behaviour holds for a metered group.
findings.text: §10 says a group whose every member is review-excluded withholds no bookend reserve, but line 1924 in the same section says the opposite for exactly those groups ("`review_excluded_backends` lists every metered lane, so on those lanes only the `verify` role can spend that reserve. Up to a fifth of each metered window therefore expires unspent"), and §8 (:1082) states the metered lane's bookends — reviews *and* verifications — "are reserved" and rely on §4's reserve; §5b's landed figure (:850) likewise draws the metered wallet `codex-sub` with "a 20% reserve withheld from the start of the window", yet the workstation's own `review_excluded_backends` excludes all four of that wallet's members (codex, codex-astra, codex-luna, codex-tera) plus codex-spark, so under §10's rule that wallet withholds none

findings.reason: the section's own done-when tests a lift above `max_multiple` and one older than `max_hours`, both of which pass against the default values with the keys never wired, so without an assertion that a flight layer writing either key is accepted and moves the boundary the deliverable is unmeasured.
findings.text: the change declares `budget.lift.max_multiple` (3.0) and `max_hours` (168) as `BudgetConfig` slots "so a flight layer can set them", but §10's done-when (:1950) only asserts that `bookend_reserve_pct` is accepted by the schema and moves the boundary, and asserts nothing of the kind for the two lift ceilings declared in the same sentence; since the prior defect on this key set was that they were not settable flight keys, this deliverable can pass without the wiring being shown
